predecessors.note: The Yueban descend from the Northern Xiongnu who fled west after the Xianbei campaigns of 155-166; 'Xiongnu migrations (93 CE - circa 380 CE) westward to southern Siberia and Central Asia'.

correction.text: Zhetysu, where the Yueban 'conquered Zhetysu, where they established the principality of Yueban', without the Wusun's Issyk-Kul

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. 'The Yueban conquered Zhetysu, where they established the principality of Yueban' (undated); the Yueban were in Zhetysu, 'now part of modern-day Kazakhstan'. The Wusun shape of 91 (Issyk-Kul) is subtracted because the wusun dossier keeps the Wusun there to 450. The infobox starts the principality in 160, the date of the Xianbei campaigns (155-166), not of the conquest of Zhetysu; the page gives no area.

ledger.note: c. 160: the Yueban principality. Infobox 'Established: 160'; 'Between 155 and 166, the Xianbei ... conducted a series of campaigns against Northern Xiongnu' who fled west. The page dates no conquest of Zhetysu: the infobox year is taken, with the Zhetysu land as the researcher's reading (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 480s-490: the Yueban principality ends. 'The Yueban principality ceased to existed during the 480s and split into four tribes' (text); infobox 'Disestablished: 490'. In 448 Northern Wei received an envoy from the Yueban; late in the 5th century the Yueban 'were attacked by the Tiele'.

wars.note: The Hephthalites conquered the Tiele in 495-496 (page).

certainty.note: A steppe principality; the page names Zhetysu and the Tarbagatai range but no border.

sources.title: Yueban
sources.note: Infobox 160 to 490; Xianbei campaigns 155-166; the Xiongnu migrations; Zhetysu; the 448 envoy; the Tiele attack; the 480s end.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Yueban; ia-01-a asked for 91-490). One page opened. The page gives 93 CE for the start of the Xiongnu migrations where ia-01-a assumed 91; the infobox 160 is a date of the Xianbei war, so the real start is unsettled and the Zhetysu shape is soft. The Wusun dossier keeps the Wusun on Issyk-Kul to 450, so the Yueban shape subtracts the Wusun's Cliopatria shape of 91; the Ili valley the Wusun held before 91 is not claimed by the Yueban here. Successors: none on the page (four tribes; the Hephthalites after 495). Gazetteer names used (Semirechye) resolve.
